title: Earthquake: Drop, Cover, and Hold On
summary: Immediate protocol during violent seismic shaking. Do not run outside during shaking.
criticalSteps: DROP to your hands and knees immediately to prevent being knocked down.
COVER your head and neck under a sturdy table, desk, or against an interior wall.
HOLD ON to your shelter until shaking stops completely.
If in bed, stay there, curl face down, and cover your head with a pillow.
Beware of aftershocks, which often follow within 10 to 60 minutes.
dos: Move away from windows, heavy mirrors, hanging lamps, and tall furniture.
If outdoors, move to an open area away from power lines, buildings, and sinkholes.
Turn off gas and main electricity breakers if you smell gas or see sparks.
donts: DO NOT use elevators under any circumstances.
DO NOT stand in a doorway; modern doorways are not reinforced shelters.
DO NOT run outside while shaking is occurring; falling facade glass is the #1 killer.

title: Structural Collapse & Trapped Victim Protocol
summary: Survival tactics when pinned, trapped under concrete rubble, or in void spaces.
criticalSteps: Protect your airway: Cover nose and mouth with cloth, shirt, or handkerchief to filter silica dust.
Conserve oxygen: Slow your breathing. Panic consumes limited pocket air 3x faster.
Avoid continuous shouting; shout only when you hear search teams or rescue dogs nearby.
Tap rhythmically on metal pipes, beams, or concrete in sets of 3 (SOS signal: tap-tap-tap).
Activate PulseTrack BLE Mesh or SOS siren beacon if phone is reachable.
dos: Inspect your immediate surroundings for secondary collapse hazards.
Keep phone screen brightness at absolute minimum or activate Stealth Mode to preserve battery.
Bandage active bleeding immediately using torn clothing as a tourniquet or pressure wrap.
donts: DO NOT ignite matches, lighters, or open flames; gas pockets may ignite.
DO NOT kick violently against heavy support pillars; you may trigger a roof pancake.
DO NOT waste your voice shouting continuously when no search sounds are audible.

title: Flash Flood & Tsunami Evacuation
summary: Rapid rising water protocol. Water 15cm deep can sweep an adult off their feet.
criticalSteps: Immediately move to higher ground or upper floor; never stay in basements or subterranean garages.
Turn off gas and main circuit breakers before water infiltrates the building.
If trapped in a building, climb to the roof. Do not climb into a closed attic without an exit tool.
Never drive into floodwaters: Turn Around, Don't Drown. 30cm of moving water floats most cars.
dos: Wear life jackets or carry buoyant objects (coolers, sealed empty plastic containers).
Stay informed via battery-powered emergency radios or PulseTrack offline alerts.
Signal rescuers with bright colored cloth or flashing phone torch from the rooftop.
donts: DO NOT attempt to walk through fast-moving water.
DO NOT touch downed electrical wires or submerged appliances.
DO NOT return to your home until authorities confirm structural safety.

title: High-Rise Fire & Smoke Infiltration
summary: Smoke inhalation kills faster than flames. Stay low beneath the thermal toxic layer.
criticalSteps: Drop to your hands and knees: clean air remains within 30cm of the floor.
Feel door handles with the back of your hand. If hot, DO NOT open the door.
If path is clear, evacuate via emergency fire stairwells. Close doors behind you to compartmentalize fire.
If trapped in a room, seal door cracks and vents with wet towels, sheets, or duct tape.
dos: Breathe through a wet cotton cloth to cool air and trap soot particles.
Hang a bright cloth or sheet out the window to signal ladder trucks.
Call emergency services (112 / 911) and inform them of your exact floor and room number.
donts: DO NOT use elevators; electrical failure could trap you in the shaft.
DO NOT break windows unless absolutely necessary; opening windows introduces oxygen and draws smoke.
DO NOT re-enter a burning building for pets or personal possessions.

title: Active Threat & Hostile Encounter (Run, Hide, Fight)
summary: Tactical survival guidelines during an active shooter, armed assailant, or urban unrest.
criticalSteps: RUN: If there is an accessible escape path, evacuate immediately. Leave belongings behind.
HIDE: If escape is impossible, lock and barricade the door with heavy furniture.
STEALTH: Mute your phone completely, turn off vibration, switch PulseTrack to OLED Stealth Mode.
FIGHT: As an absolute last resort when your life is in imminent danger, act aggressively to incapacitate the threat.
dos: Stay low, away from windows, doors, and sightlines.
Spread out if with others; do not huddle together in a cluster.
Keep hands visible, palms open, and fingers spread when law enforcement arrives.
donts: DO NOT make sudden movements toward officers or point at them.
DO NOT make any noise, ringtone, or screen flash while in concealment.
DO NOT open the door for anyone until official security forces are clearly confirmed.

title: Trauma First Aid: Hemorrhage Control & CPR
summary: Stopping severe arterial bleeding and maintaining cardiac perfusion until medics arrive.
criticalSteps: Check responsiveness and breathing: If unresponsive with no normal breathing, begin CPR immediately.
CPR: Push hard and fast in center of chest (100-120 bpm, 5cm deep) to the beat of 'Stayin' Alive'.
Arterial Bleeding: Apply direct, hard pressure directly onto the wound with sterile gauze or clean cloth.
Tourniquet: For catastrophic limb bleeding, place 5-7cm above wound (never over a joint). Tighten windlass until bleeding stops.
dos: Pack deep penetrating wounds with clean cloth or gauze before applying pressure.
Keep the victim warm with blankets or clothing to prevent hypothermia and coagulopathy.
Note the exact time a tourniquet was applied on the patient's forehead (e.g. 'TK 14:30').
donts: DO NOT loosen or remove a tourniquet once applied; only hospital surgeons should remove it.
DO NOT remove embedded foreign objects (knives, glass shards); stabilize them in place.
DO NOT give food or drink to an unconscious victim or someone needing surgery.
